issues.description: build.R loads neiUS.rdata and relies on ghgNeiUS with facility/process rows and matching keys. The release contains neither the prepared object nor code specifying the documented upstream FRS/name/coordinate/industry matching. The public NEI and EIS systems are distinct and cannot be assumed to reproduce this author object.
The active US parent-company and namesByHand.csv inputs are absent. Highest-level owner decisions, gvkey/orgType joins and preserved Canadian name path are required for the main panel.

The supplied source contains a full commented Stan model block and explicitly instructs the reader to place it in myStan.stan. The separate file is absent, so it must be materialized in a working copy. RStan documentation permits unused extra data-list objects, and build.R computes new-sample predictions in R from beta draws; logYNew appears only in the pars save selector and is not consumed downstream. Removing that unused selector name is a source-supported same-model cleanup. Exact author RStan-version behavior is not runtime-verified.

The active Table 7 branch jointly requires dataSimilarity (jacOld/jacNew), dataIndSimilarity (groupVar/jacMean) and dataChJac (idFrs/chJacAbove/chJacBelow). Appendix A8 supplies the representative state-industry peer and weighted Jaccard formula; code supplies the NAICS4/state group and intensity thresholds. Its comments tie 2010 to the carbon-light peer comparison and describe the analogous >0.67 carbon-intense peers as in 2013; the complete row/year/peer construction of the output objects remains unspecified. build.R has no local assignment or explicit load for these names in the Table 7 branch, but earlier load() calls can introduce additional objects and those RData namespaces were not inspected; static review therefore cannot establish that the prepared objects are absent. The exact prepared-object container or separate manual producer/schema route remains unresolved.

The code computes a DSIRE candidate and comments that it should be exported for manual review, then reads regsByHand.csv; no export or review-decision record is supplied. The Canadian regsCanada.csv is separately described as a hand-coded NRCan table.
The required 1976-2020-senate.csv has no identified source or format contract in the package; the code needs state, year, candidatevotes and candidate to select 2004–2012 winners.

The prepared compustat.rdata and compForCdp.Rdata are absent. A local COMP.FUNDA candidate confirms some raw annual fields, but does not establish the prepared year, market value, NAICS, ZIP, notes, sample and firm mappings required by the two code branches.

The package contains build.R and documentation but not the required source files, prepared RData objects, manual crosswalks, historical policy/vote/CDP files or verified contracts for the three Table 7 similarity objects and any separate producer. The Stan source itself is included inline with an explicit instruction to stage it as myStan.stan, so this is preparation rather than a missing model-source blocker. Earlier RData object namespaces were not inspected; routes for dataSimilarity, dataIndSimilarity and dataChJac remain unknown rather than proven absent. Most other data routes remain unverified; exact author inputs and contracts must be recovered before full-pipeline execution can be assessed.

evidence.description: The main program reads eight US GHGRP annual direct-emitter files and adds their reporting year.
The program reads Canadian GHGRP data, maps facility/owner/geographic/emissions fields, filters years, and binds it with US records.
The program reads the US parent-company file and namesByHand.csv, selects ownership above 50 percent, cleans names and joins the manual mapping.
The program loads neiUS.rdata, documents the NEI/EIS year sets and states that its FRS/name/coordinate/industry match is upstream.
evidence.quote:
#* Create GHGRP-NEI/EIS file ---------------------------------------------------
load("neiUS.rdata");
  # loads CO data from US NEI (2008, 2011, 2014) and EIS data (2009, 2010, 2012,
  # 2013) provided directly by US EPA

  # The next steps match NEI/EIS data with US GHGRP data by first using EPA
  # identifiers obtained through an EPA FRS query. For unmatched observations,
  # I then match using facility name, geo coordinates, and industry. I only use
  # GHGRP observations where the FRS ID matches 1:N with a GHGRP facility, and
  # NEI/EIS observations where the FRS ID matches 1:N with an NEI/EIS facility.
  # This lets me later add the emissions of different GHGRP facilities within an
  # FRS ID. The outputted object is "ghgNeiUS."

evidence.description: The appendix defines the US NEI/EIS source unit as facility-process-pollutant emissions and identifies the SCC process families.
evidence.quote:
A proxy for the quantity of goods produced is provided by the US EPA’s National Emis-
sions Inventory and Emissions Inventory System (US NEI/EIS). The US NEI/EIS contains
data about (non-GHG) facility-process-pollutant level emissions and spans a wide range
of industries. In 2013, at least 57% of US Program facilities in my sample also reported
to the US NEI/EIS.4 A US NEI/EIS processe is identified by an eight-digit Source Clas-
sification Code (SCC). SCCs beginning with “1’, “2”, and “5” describe fuel-combustion
processes. For example, SCC 10300221 refers to External Combustion Boilers: Commer-
cial/Institutional: Bituminous/Subbituminous Coal: Pulverized Coal: Wet Bottom (Subbi-
tuminous Coal). SCCs beginning with “3” and “4” denote non-combustion processes (US
EPA, 2021). For example, SCC 30700651 refers to Industrial Processes: Pulp and Paper and
Wood Products: Particleboard Manufacture: Batch Hot Press, Urea Formaldehyde Resin.

evidence.description: The program contains a commented Stan model block and then calls stan(file="myStan.stan") with current and new-sample data and requests logYNew.
evidence.quote:
# For the step below, place the following in text file called "myStan.stan":
# data {
#   int n; // number of obs
#   int kYesPriors; // number of processes with priors
#   int kNoPriors; // number of processes with NO priors
#   
#   matrix[n, kYesPriors] xYesPriors; // the model matrix with priors
#   matrix[n, kNoPriors] xNoPriors; // the model matrix with NO priors
#   
#   int j; // number of priors
#   vector[j] priorsMean; // emission factors
#   vector[j] priorsVar; // emission factors
#   
#   real logY[n]; // co2
# }
# 
# parameters {
#   vector<lower=0>[kYesPriors] betaYesPriors; // regression parame with priors
#   vector<lower=0>[kNoPriors] betaNoPriors; // regression parame with NO priors
#   
#   real <lower=0> sigmaSq; // the standard deviation
# }
# 
# transformed parameters {
#   vector[n] logLinPredMean;
#   real<lower=0> sigma;
#   
#   logLinPredMean = log(xYesPriors * betaYesPriors + xNoPriors * betaNoPriors);
#   sigma = sqrt(sigmaSq);
# }
# 
# model {  
#   betaYesPriors ~ lognormal(priorsMean, priorsVar); // populated with data
#   betaNoPriors ~ lognormal(1*log(3347.719)/2, (2*log(3347.719)/2)^0.5); // populated with parameters
#   
#   sigmaSq ~ inv_gamma(1, 1);
#   logY ~ normal(logLinPredMean, sigma);
# }

stanFit <- stan(file= "myStan.stan", data =
                  list(n= nrow(xYesPriors),
                       kYesPriors= ncol(xYesPriors),
                       kNoPriors= ncol(xNoPriors),
                       xYesPriors= xYesPriors,
                       xNoPriors= xNoPriors,
                       xYesPriorsNew= xYesPriorsNew,
                       xNoPriorsNew= xNoPriorsNew,
                       nNew= nrow(xYesPriorsNew),
                       kYesPriorsNew= ncol(xYesPriorsNew),
                       kNoPriorsNew= ncol(xNoPriorsNew),
                       j= length(priorsVar),
                       priorsMean= priorsMean,
                       priorsVar= priorsVar,
                       logY= logY),
                iter=iter,
                chains=nchains,
                pars = c("betaYesPriors", "betaNoPriors", "sigma", "logYNew"),
                control = list(adapt_delta = 0.8,
                               max_treedepth = 12));

data <- merge(
  ghgProc, data.table(ghgNeiUS)[, c("idGhg", "ghg", "co2NonBio", "state"):= NULL],
  by= c("idFrs", "year"));

# As per Section 5.4 and Online Appendix A8, I used "data" to compute facility-
# level process similarity for facilities and their peers in 2010 and 2013.
# These appear as "jacOld" and "jacNew" in outputted object "dataSimilarity." A
# peer group's mean similarity in 2010 appears as "jacMean" in outputted
# object "dataIndSimilarity." I then compute a facility-level similarity in
# 2010, but limiting peer facilities to those with carbon intensity <= 0.33
# (carbon light). I then compute the change in similarity when considering
# facilities in 2013 and their 2010 carbon light peers. I also compute the
# analagous change in similarity when considering peers with carbon intensity
# > 0.67 in 2013 (carbon intense). These changes appear as "chJacAbove" and
# "chJacBelow" in outputted object "dataChJac."

review_notes: Scope is the complete supplied build.R program and its active Table 1–9 and model branches. The author-commented Table 3 column 4 shortcut is not the assessed target. identifiers.txt is documented as Table 4 Column 3 sample IDs, not a full panel; its values were not inspected.

No author code, dataset, Stan model, statistical/descriptive trial, or SAS runtime was executed. Successful checks were bounded software metadata, one COMP.FUNDA row without displayed values, frozen catalog metadata, and official static product/API documentation only.

The model source is included in build.R at lines 623–659, with an explicit instruction to save it as myStan.stan. RStan documentation supports omitting unused extra data objects and defines pars as a saved-parameter selector; code computes new-sample predictions from beta draws in R. The proposal removes only the unused logYNew selector name; exact author RStan-version behavior and model execution remain untested.

Appendix A8 supplies the representative state-industry peer and weighted Jaccard process-similarity formula. Code further specifies NAICS4/state grouping; its comments tie the carbon-light (<=0.33) comparison to 2013 facilities and their 2010 peers, then describe the analogous carbon-intense (>0.67) peers as in 2013. The actual unresolved Table 7 gap is the missing executable producer or loaded dataSimilarity/dataIndSimilarity/dataChJac objects and any remaining implementation details the supplied recipe does not resolve.

US and Canadian GHGRP field normalization and identifiers, manual owner matching, NEI versus EIS versus NPRI distinctions, SNL/AER gas pricing, prepared research inputs, policy coding, and CDP manual mapping remain explicitly separate.
